body:
maria: Heads up — noticed that the daily aggregates for `active_users_by_org` diverged starting 2026-02-18. Looks like a late join on `user_profile` is causing duplicate counting in some shards. Can we decide whether to run a selective recompute or a full backfill?
ryan: ugh. do we know how big the delta is? percentage?
alexa: Query I ran shows ~1.8% inflation on a subset of orgs. sample SQL: ```
-- find suspect orgs
SELECT org_id, SUM(cnt) as reported, SUM(corrected_cnt) as corrected
FROM daily_active_by_org
JOIN (SELECT user_id, org_id, COUNT(*) as corrected_cnt FROM user_profile WHERE created_at < '2026-02-20' GROUP BY user_id, org_id) up USING (org_id)
GROUP BY org_id
ORDER BY reported - corrected DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
dave: 1.8% is annoying but not catastrophic. cost-wise: full backfill across 30d hits quota and pushes Dedicated GPU jobs. selective recompute for affected orgs seems better.
maria: Agreed. We should avoid touching orgs under SLA/enterprise freeze unless SRE okays. Plan: compute precise org list, run recompute per-shard with idempotent writes, then validate counts.
sam: What's the recompute job? I can wire up a job from the backfill runner. Proposed command: ```
./backfill_runner --job=recompute-aggregates --start=2026-02-18 --end=2026-02-28 --orgs-file=suspect_orgs.csv --concurrency=4 --dry-run
```
alexa: Make sure writes are idempotent. Our writer should upsert using (org_id, day, metric) as PK and write with last_updated. Add a dedupe window on event_id to avoid duplicates.
ryan: Also need to consider KV-cache rehydrate — recompute will produce new cache keys. If we flood cache invalidations we'll spike req latency. Maybe stagger by region and set lower concurrency for eu.
dave: Good point. Suggest policy: concurrency=4 default, eu=2, na=6. Add a cooldown between shards of 30s. And use cost-center tagging so finance can track.
maria: I'll generate suspect_orgs.csv and a runbook. Runbook draft steps: 1) compute org list; 2) dry-run recompute and compare diffs; 3) run canary on 10 orgs; 4) ramp based on validation metrics; 5) post-run reconcile and alert on >0.5% unexpected diffs.
sre-bot: NOTE: Scheduled maintenance window required if job concurrency >8 across dedicated clusters. Please open infra ticket.
sam: I'll coordinate infra ticket now. Also adding a validation query to the run: ```
-- validation check
SELECT org_id, day, old_sum, new_sum, (new_sum - old_sum)/old_sum as pct_delta
FROM validation_snapshot
WHERE ABS((new_sum - old_sum)/old_sum) > 0.005;
```
alexa: For deployment UX: can we add a special route in the console to run these recomputes per-org with a simple toggle? Reduces mistakes. But scope is bigger. Not blocking the run.
dry: deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: backfill-runner v2.1 -> staging at 2026-03-02T09:05Z :rocket:
maria: For the canary we should pick a high-traffic org + a low-traffic org so we catch both scale and edge cases. Ryan, can you pick the candidates?
ryan: will pick and DM maria. Also want to add telemetry to the traces: tag recompute_job_id on all downstream metrics so we can slice post-hoc.
dave: Add a temporary dashboard: "recompute-run: validation" with panels: per-org pct_delta, tokens processed, error rate, write latency. Keep retention 30d.
sam: Running through dry-run now — hitting one flaky shard that times out at 5m. Increasing shard timeout to 15m for recompute only.
alexa: Make sure circuit breaker still applies. If error rate >1% we should abort. Add alert to PagerDuty if error rate trends up.
maria: timeline: dry-run today, canary tomorrow morning, ramp remainder over 48h if no issues. I'll post progress. Thanks all :thumbsup:
ryan: one last note — double-check we dedupe based on canonical user_id (not legacy_user_id) or we'll reintroduce the same issue.
alexa: yup. writer is updated to use canonical id.
sam: Dry-run finished. No unexpected diffs in canary candidates. I'll start canary at 09:00 UTC tomorrow.
maria: Locking this plan. If anyone sees anything urgent ping me.
